hard.meaning: Blocks release because failure creates legal, compliance, security, build, routing, source, or publication-integrity risk.

strong_soft.meaning: Does not block artifact handoff, but must be visible because it materially affects production readiness or operator follow-through.

warning.meaning: Advisory quality or optimization issue. It should not block release unless it accumulates into a strategic or user-facing risk.

pettyBlockerPolicy: Cosmetic preferences, optional metadata improvements, minor wording preferences, and low-impact optimization gaps may warn but must not hard-fail release.

validators.risk: Pre-license site cannot publish licensed treatment claims or activate sensitive capabilities.
Approved scheduled content must be complete, dated, source-aware, disclaimer-aware, and eligible before autopublish.
Required legal pages and mode-specific disclaimers must exist.
AEO/SEO/GEO strategy must include query, answer, entity, route, atom, market, and public answer surfaces.
Client-facing pages, admin controls, native publishing code, and original 2026 editorial identity must not drift.
Distribution must follow existing publication and never fabricate provider success.
Future content must be deterministic, diverse, append-only, licensure-safe, and visible in the unchanged admin flow.
Canonicals, sitemap and robots pointing at another host hand every page to a different site.
Pages without their own title/description or a definition paragraph lose snippet and answer-engine eligibility.
Clarity must be keyed by hostname and load only after analytics consent.
A key file that does not match the key makes every IndexNow submission fail.
Built pages missing favicon, og:image, twitter card or self-canonical.
Built pages missing LocalBusiness/WebSite/WebPage/Breadcrumb JSON-LD or claiming invisible FAQ.
A local service page without a callable phone link loses the lead.
The sitemap must list only pages that render: published blog items and live search-loop question pages, none missing; published items must be structurally complete.
